title: Carbon dioxide and methane as greenhouse gases

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: long wavelength radiation
items.clue: Given off by the warmed surface of the Earth.

items.label: short wavelength radiation
items.clue: Arrives from the Sun and mostly passes straight through the atmosphere.

items.label: peer review
items.clue: Checking of methods, data and conclusions by other scientists before publication.

items.label: greenhouse gas
items.clue: Absorbs energy radiated by the surface of the Earth and sends some of it back down.

questions.stem: Which statement about greenhouse gases in the Earth's atmosphere is correct?

options.text: Water vapour, carbon dioxide and methane are all greenhouse gases.
Water vapour is a natural gas and so is not a greenhouse gas.
Only gases released by human activity act as greenhouse gases.
Greenhouse gases make up most of the atmosphere by volume.

questions.explanation: These are the three greenhouse gases the specification names.

questions.stem: Which human activity increases the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?

options.text: Growing rice in fields that are kept flooded all year.
Keeping large herds of cattle on grassland.
Burying more household waste in landfill sites.
Burning fossil fuels in power stations and vehicles.

questions.explanation: Combustion of fossil fuels is a named human source of carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Why is a rise of about one degree in the average global temperature important?

options.text: Every place on Earth is now one degree warmer.
It shifts the climate of the whole Earth.
It is too small to change the weather at all.
It shows that the ozone layer is thinning.

questions.explanation: An average across the whole planet moving is a large change to the climate system.

questions.stem: What is the carbon footprint of a product?

options.text: Carbon dioxide given off while the product is made.
Greenhouse gases emitted over its full life cycle.
The mass of carbon that the finished object contains.
The carbon dioxide released while the product is used.

questions.explanation: The definition covers carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases across the whole life cycle.

questions.stem: What do greenhouse gases in the atmosphere do for living things on Earth?

options.text: They block the ultraviolet radiation coming from the Sun.
They pollute the air and are harmful to all living things.
They cool the Earth by reflecting sunlight into space.
They keep temperatures on Earth high enough to support life.

questions.explanation: This is exactly what the specification says greenhouse gases maintain.

questions.stem: Explain why cutting down large areas of forest increases the amount of carbon dioxide in the air.

options.text: Trees give out carbon dioxide, so cutting them down helps the air.
Cutting the trees down releases the methane that is stored in wood.
Fewer trees are left to remove carbon dioxide by photosynthesis.
Losing trees thins the ozone layer and lets more heat in.

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process that takes carbon dioxide out of the air, so removing trees reduces it.

questions.stem: Which of these is a potential effect of global climate change?

options.text: Sea level rise, causing flooding of low-lying land.
More acid rain falling on lakes and forests.
A larger hole in the ozone layer each spring.
An increase in deforestation and cattle farming.

questions.explanation: Rising sea level and flooding are named potential effects.

questions.stem: Which statement about a carbon footprint is correct?

options.text: It includes methane as well as carbon dioxide, at every stage.
It counts carbon dioxide only, from the factory stage.
It is the carbon locked inside the finished product.
It counts only the gases given off during its transport.

questions.explanation: The definition covers carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases, over the full life cycle.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the greenhouse effect?

options.text: Long wavelength radiation passes through and short wavelength is absorbed.
Greenhouse gases reflect the incoming radiation back down to the ground.
Short wavelength radiation passes through; long wavelength is absorbed.
Greenhouse gases hold warm air near the ground, like a blanket.

questions.explanation: Solar radiation passes through the atmosphere, and the long wavelength radiation emitted by the surface is absorbed by greenhouse gases.

questions.stem: Which pair of human activities both increase the amount of methane in the atmosphere?

options.text: Landfill sites and burning of coal.
Cattle farming and rice growing.
Deforestation and cattle farming.
Aerosol sprays and air conditioning.

questions.explanation: Livestock and flooded rice fields are both named methane sources.

questions.stem: Which list contains only potential effects of global climate change?

options.text: Flooding, deforestation, more frequent storms and stronger winds.
Rising sea level, acid rain, changes to rainfall patterns.
Extreme weather, cattle farming, loss of some habitats.
Flooding, more extreme weather, changes to species distribution.

questions.explanation: All three are potential effects the specification expects students to describe.

questions.stem: A company wants to reduce the carbon footprint of its factory. Which action would do this?

options.text: Fit filters to the chimneys to trap all the carbon dioxide.
Cut emissions only during manufacture.
Make the product from materials containing less carbon.
Take the factory's electricity from wind and solar farms.

questions.explanation: Renewable electricity replaces fossil fuel combustion, so less carbon dioxide is emitted.
